maria (platform): Heads-up — we're rolling out the new runtime dashboards for model-serving. Need to lock down alerting rules & pager routing before we enable evals. cc @kevin @jon

jon (eng-sre): +1. What metrics are we planning to alert on? p95 latency, 5xx rate, SLO burn?

maria (platform): Proposed list: p95_latency_ms per route/model, error_rate_5xx, slo_burn_ratio (30m and 1h), batch_queue_length, kv_cache_hit_rate. Default thresholds: p95 > 600ms for 5m -> warning, 1200ms for 3m -> page; 5xx > 0.5% sustained 10m -> page; slo_burn > 3x in 30m -> page. Thoughts?

alex (eng-runtime): batch_queue_length will be key. If queue > 100 for 2m it's a capacity issue. kv_cache_hit_rate < 80% often means cold starts. Also add `prefetch_blocked` counter for downstream stalls.

jon (eng-sre): Paging policy idea: capacity alerts (queue, node_p95 with high gpu_util) -> infra oncall. Functional/regression alerts (slo burn without saturation) -> platform oncall. Use labels like `team=infra` or `team=platform` on alerts to drive routing.

kevin (oncall): Agree. Concretize thresholds: prefer a low-noise warning path first. Example: p95>600ms -> notify #oncall-warn (no PD page) if 5m; escalate to PD if p95>1200ms for 3m. Also want stale-alert suppression during planned rollouts.

rachael (eng-platform): Add `suppress_during_rollout=true` tag we can set at deployment time. Also annotate rules with runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving.

maria (platform): I'll draft rules. quick snippet: 

```yaml
- alert: ModelServingHighP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model))
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving
```

jon (eng-sre): For SLO burn use existing metric `slo/burn_rate{window="1h"}`. Page if burn_rate > 4 for 30m. We'll add a derived alert `ModelServingSLOBurn30m`.

alex (eng-runtime): When alerts fire, include `model_sha`, `node_p95`, and `gpu_util` in the payload/labels so oncall gets immediate context. We'll export those metrics.

kevin (oncall): PD routing: infra incidents -> PD policy `infra-pd`; platform incidents -> `platform-pd`. Jon — can you own PD setup?

jon (eng-sre): Yep. I need the final alert names + labels from you, Maria. I'll wire alertmanager routes and test with `alertmanager.test`. Also recommend `noisy_route=true` tag for experiment routes so we can mute them.

maria (platform): Planned alert names: ModelServingHighP95, ModelServing5xxRate, ModelServingSLOBurn30m, BatchQueueCapacity, KVCacheColdStart, PrefetchBlockedSpike.

metrics-bot: Draft dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/model-serving-runtime :eyes:

kevin (oncall): I'll run a dry-run paging test tomorrow 09:00 PT. Reply here if you want to be included.

rachael (eng-platform): Ack, include me. Also let's add a 15m auto-escalation to platform oncall for repeated warnings.

maria (platform): Action items:
- maria: push alert rules draft (PR)
- jon: configure PD routing + run test
- alex: ensure metrics exported with requested labels
- kevin: run paging test tomorrow 09:00 PT
I'll post PR link in this thread when ready.

deploy-bot: Created PR #789 in infra/alerting: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/789

jon (eng-sre): I'll review PR today. Recommend adding a `suppress_during_rollout` template and a `noisy_route` label for experiments. Also add `severity: warning|page` and `team` labels consistently.

kevin (oncall): :thumbsup:

maria (platform): Keeping thresholds conservative for now to avoid noisy pages. Will iterate after the first test. Ping if objections.

kevin (oncall): Thanks — see you at the dry-run.
